topics.title: Revenue, margins and customers
topics.one_liner: Q2 2026 revenue was $11.5B recognized, 14x YoY, but the $65B run-rate is gross and the record's 6-10% haircut evidence sits far below the desk's 39.75%.

key_metrics.label: Latest run-rate (outlet-reported)
key_metrics.value: $65B+ at end-July 2026, gross basis, 7.2x end-2025's $9B. Bloomberg via TechCrunch (T2), FT and Axios agree. Last company-stated figure: $47B in May (T1). Nothing above $65B is verified.

key_metrics.label: FY2025 recognized revenue
key_metrics.value: $4.59B, +1,088% YoY, gross of cloud resale. FY2024 about $0.39B, implied. Exit run-rates were $9B and $1B. Leaked draft prospectus via Reuters (T2), no public S-1.

key_metrics.label: Q2 2026 revenue
key_metrics.value: $11.5B recognized, 14x YoY and 2.4x Q1's $4.73B. H1 2026 is $16.2B. Leaked draft (T2). Beat the May 20 projection of $10.9B by 5.5%.

key_metrics.label: Gross margin, by definition
key_metrics.value: Above 80% adjusted, before partner share and training (FT, T3). About 40% for FY2025 (The Information, T3). About 44% for Q2 2026E (PitchBook, T3). No GAAP gross margin reported.

key_metrics.label: Channel share
key_metrics.value: 47% of FY2025 sales, $2.16B, through Amazon and Google marketplaces, up from 11% in 2023. Platforms kept about $351M, 7.6% of revenue (Reuters-computed, T3 in the prospectus table).

key_metrics.label: Customer concentration
key_metrics.value: Two unnamed customers at 12% each, about 24% of FY2025 revenue (T2). Most large customers lack long-term contracts (T3). The 1,000 customers above $1M floor only $1B, 1.5% of run-rate.

what.t: Run-rate path. Anthropic stated $9B at end-2025, $14B on Feb 12, above $30B on Apr 6 and above $47B in May (T1, gross basis inferred). Bloomberg via TechCrunch, Aug 17 (T2) reported above $65B at end-July, with FT and Axios agreeing. Nothing higher is verified. The $100B to $120B year-end figures from Quartz, FT, WSJ and the NYT via Gulf News (T4) are projections.

Recognized revenue. Reuters and Fortune read a leaked draft prospectus, Sep 28 to 29 (T2, single origin, no public S-1). The event is DISPUTED in the record because two periods share one field. FY2024 was near $0.39B, implied, and FY2025 $4.59B. Q1 2026 was $4.73B and Q2 $11.5B, 14x a year earlier. H1 2026 is $16.2B, 3.5x FY2025. The FY2025 operating loss was $8.06B, up from $2.98B.

Channel and customers. Reuters, Sep 29 (T3 in the prospectus table): Amazon and Google marketplaces carried 47% of FY2025 sales, $2.16B, up from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024. Anthropic books them gross as principal. Platforms kept about 16 cents per dollar, $351M, 7.6% of revenue. Two unnamed customers were 12% each. Most large customers lack long-term contracts.

Margins. Every figure has a different scope. The Information, Jan 21 (T3): FY2025 about 40%, below a 50% plan. FT, Sep 13 (T3): above 80% in Q2 2026 before partner share and training. PitchBook, Sep 16 (T3): about 44%. Adjusted operating income was positive in Q2 with no dollar amount. The $559M was a May 20 projection.

Mix. FY2025 revenue was $3.8B usage-based and $789M subscription, 17.2% (T2). Business was about 80% of sales (T4, Oct 2025). Claude Code run-rate rose from $1B in Nov 2025 to above $2.5B in Feb 2026, 18% of run-rate, no later figure (T1). Enterprise moved to a $20 seat plus API-rate usage (The Register, T2). Menlo, an Anthropic investor, gave Anthropic 54% of enterprise coding (T3).

Comparables. OpenAI's FY2025 revenue was $13.07B net of Microsoft share (T3) and its Q2 2026 $6.2B (WSJ via Proactive, basis unstated), against Anthropic's gross $11.5B. xAI booked $3.2B in FY2025 (T2). The 2028 plan went from $70B with $17B of cash flow (Nov 2025, T3, DISPUTED in the record for mixed fields) to $190B to $200B (Reuters, Aug 17, T2), with no cash-flow figure for the new plan.

means.t: A run-rate annualizes a recent period, so recognized revenue lags it in a fast ramp. FY2025 revenue was 0.51x the $9B exit run-rate and FY2024 was 0.39x. Desk-derived trailing revenue is about $19.6B, 0.30x of $65B (LOW). Growth is slowing: the pace fell from about $13B added a month from April to mid-May to about $7B a month since, 13.5% a month.

Anthropic books marketplace sales gross as principal, with the platform share in marketing expense. The haircut is take rate times channel share: 16 cents times 47% is 7.6%, and 16% at full share. A 39.75% haircut needs platforms to keep 85 cents per marketplace dollar and implies $4.6B paid away in Q2, against $1.9B forecast for all of 2026 (The Information, Feb). The record has no derivation.

Margins differ in scope. PitchBook's 44% equals one minus its projected $0.56 Q2 compute ratio ($0.71 in Q1), so it deducts only compute. The above-80% figure drops partner share and training. If $0.56 is all-in compute and inference is 37% of it, as The Information's 2026 plan implies, inference costs about $0.21 per dollar, near 80% (desk arithmetic). The ratio was $1.60 in FY2025.

Volume carries growth as prices fall. Sep 30 list prices per million tokens: Haiku $1/$5, Sonnet $2/$10, Opus $4/$20, Fable $10/$50. Opus fell 67% in Nov 2025 and 20% on Sep 22. A 20% cut needs 25% more tokens to hold revenue, a 67% cut needs 3x. Tokenizers add up to 35% more tokens, offsetting part of each cut. No volume series is in the record.

implications.t: Carry both haircuts until the S-1 fixes the basis. End-July net run-rate is $58.5B to $61.1B at 6% to 10%, and $39.2B at 39.75%. Applying the FY2025 fee ratio, Q2's $11.5B is 1.7x OpenAI's $6.2B (WSJ, basis unstated) at 7.6% and 1.1x at 39.75%. Do not plot the two labs' run-rates on one axis.

Label the denominator on every multiple. A reported $2T IPO target is 30.8x the gross end-July run-rate, 32.7x to 34.2x net of 6% to 10%, 43.5x Q2 annualized recognized revenue and about 10x the 2028 projection midpoint. Reuters' 18x to 20x states no revenue basis. Never apply a recognized-revenue multiple to run-rate.

Discount quality for concentration until names and terms appear. Two customers are about 24% of FY2025 revenue, and most large ones lack long-term contracts. Amazon and Google are investors, suppliers and the channel for 47% of sales. The 1,000 customers above $1M floor 1.5% of run-rate. Consumer grew an estimated 75% from January to mid-May, run-rate about 4x, so the 80% business split is stale.

Quote one margin only with its definition. Treat above 80% as a management view, 40% and 44% as estimates and GAAP gross margin as unreported. Score Q3 on a dollar amount for adjusted operating income and a GAAP bridge. Q2 had SpaceX's two-month discount, which a T5 relay of the WSJ says ended in July, with compute costs expected to rise in H2.

second_order: Bases will be forced into the open. If the S-1 keeps gross presentation, OpenAI and sell-side comps must bridge to net. If it moves to net, every run-rate print restates by the fee share. Either way Anthropic's $65B and OpenAI's nearly $70B (Axios, basis unstated, two months later) stop being comparable headlines. PitchBook already said neither company's basis would survive a Big Four audit.

The channel grows faster than the company. The Information projected partner payouts of $360M in 2025, $1.9B in 2026 and $6.4B in 2027, up 5.3x then 3.4x. Claude Platform on AWS and Foundry bill through marketplaces, so share likely rises above 47%, and cloud providers already collect 60% of receivables. The S-1 must explain a fee line that scales.

Price cuts make revenue depend on volume from coding agents. OpenAI answered Opus 5.5 the same day with Luna at $0.10 and $0.50, one-tenth of Haiku 4.5's $1 and $5. SpaceX, which sells Anthropic $1.25B a month of compute, agreed to buy Cursor, a named Claude coding customer. Distribution, rivalry and supply meet in one counterparty, and the record does not give Cursor's current share.

The valuation-quality gap is wider than the headlines. Recognized revenue is about 0.30x of run-rate, the run-rate is gross, and two margin figures differ by 36 points. Consensus is missing that the S-1 resets all three at once, and that the last verified run-rate is two months old in a business adding about $7B a month.

Comparable data need care. OpenAI's Q2 $6.2B with +18% QoQ (WSJ) implies Q1 of $5.25B, not the $5.7B in the record. xAI's Q2 AI-segment revenue includes compute rented to a customer the desk infers is Anthropic, so part of it is Anthropic's own cost. Neither series is a clean revenue comp.

watch.item: Next run-rate print after the $65B end-July figure, company-stated or from Bloomberg, FT or Axios
watch.threshold: Below $79B at end-September is under the straight-line path to $100B at year-end. Above $87B is on the $120B path. Any figure above $100B before December would be the first actual, not a projection.

watch.item: Public S-1 income statement: audited FY2025, H1 2026, cost of revenue, gross profit and the revenue-recognition note
watch.threshold: GAAP gross margin against above 80% adjusted and 40% to 44% estimates. GAAP operating result against the adjusted figure. Any move to net presentation or a stated principal-versus-agent policy change.

watch.item: Q3 2026 results, which WSJ says Anthropic will show investors before a November listing
watch.threshold: Revenue near $17B to $18B is on the path to $100B to $120B. $20B or more runs ahead. Under $16B means the run-rate stalled after July. Adjusted operating income positive a second quarter, with a dollar amount.

watch.item: S-1 channel data: marketplace share and platform fees for H1 2026, with Microsoft Foundry broken out
watch.threshold: Share above 47% or fees above 7.6% of revenue raises the record-based haircut. A fee ratio near 39.75% would be the first evidence for the canonical figure.

watch.item: S-1 customer note: names, shares and contract terms of the largest customers, and Cursor's weight after SpaceX's $60B purchase
watch.threshold: Any customer above 10% in H1 2026. The two 12% customers unchanged or named. Share of revenue under multiyear contracts.

watch.item: Haiku 5.5 list price, promised within weeks on Sep 28
watch.threshold: Below Haiku 4.5's $1/$5 extends deflation to the small tier, where OpenAI's Luna is $0.10/$0.50. An unchanged $1/$5 holds the floor.

watch.item: OpenAI Q3 2026 revenue and a stated basis, net of Microsoft share or not
watch.threshold: Q3 against $6.2B in Q2 and a run-rate nearing $70B. A stated net basis allows a like-for-like gap. Reconcile Q1 $5.7B with the +18% QoQ claim.

watch.item: SpaceX Q3 10-Q: Customer B share of revenue and AI-segment revenue
watch.threshold: Customer B above 19.5% of revenue would show a full quarter of the Anthropic compute ramp. A named customer would settle the desk's inference.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the same $2T asks 30.8x gross run-rate or 43.5x Q2 annualized recognized revenue for margins that run from 40% to above 80% by definition, so quality cannot be ranked until the S-1 sets one basis. (b) Contradicts in size, not disproved: the record puts platform fees at 7.6% of FY2025 revenue (Reuters leak, T3) and 6% to 10% (PitchBook, T3) against 39.75%. That figure reproduces exactly as the haircut that ties $965B over $47B to $852B over $25B at 34.1x. If it was set that way, the Jul 16 tie is not independent evidence, and the $65B print has overtaken its $47B input. (c) Not tested here; the $100B to $120B year-end run-rate is an investor projection. (d) Not in this slice. (e) Confirms: run-rate, ARR and seat conventions fail when revenue is metered, booked gross and growing about 13% a month.

uncertainties.note: Every prospectus figure comes from a leaked draft that Reuters and the FT reviewed, not a filed S-1. FY2024 revenue is implied from +1,088%, not printed. The channel, fee and Q1 lines are single-chain, T3 in the prospectus table. Cost of revenue, gross profit and GAAP quarterly operating income are not reported, and the Q2 adjusted profit has no dollar amount.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The public S-1 income statement and revenue-recognition note.

uncertainties.note: The haircut is 7.6% (Reuters leak), about 7.8% on The Information's $360M, 6% to 10% (PitchBook), about 27% in an OpenAI memo that only aggregators carry (T5), and 39.75% in the desk ruling. That figure reproduces exactly as the haircut tying $965B over $47B to $852B over $25B at 34.1x, which fits a solved value, not a measured one. The record has no derivation. It may net more than fees.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A written derivation of 39.75%, the S-1 recognition note, or H1 2026 marketplace share and fees.

uncertainties.note: Margin figures share no definition: above 80% adjusted, about 40% for FY2025, 44% for Q2 2026E, a stylized inference margin above 50% from Amodei on Feb 13, and -94% in 2024 on paying users only. The compute desk reads $1.60, $0.71 and $0.56 per revenue dollar as one all-in series, while the margins table says the 2026 scope is unstated.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: An S-1 cost-of-revenue line with a training split.

uncertainties.note: Reference class in the record: Anthropic's own projections. FY2025 and Q2 2026 were beaten, year-end 2025 run-rate was met, and FY2026 is 90% reached at mid-year. No cross-company base rate is in the record. The year-end figures need $7B to $11B added a month for five months, against about $7B since May. FY2026 revenue is $35B to $44B (PitchBook, stale), $64B to $72B (desk) or $56B to $60B straight-line.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The next run-rate print and Q3 results.

uncertainties.note: Concentration is unbounded. The two 12% customers are unnamed and may overlap the 47% marketplace channel. The 1,000 customers above $1M floor only $1B. Cursor was 40% to 50% of revenue early on per one employee (T3, LOW), and SpaceX agreed to buy it (8-K, T1).
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 customer note and contract-term disclosure.

topics.title: Product, models and pricing
topics.one_liner: Opus list price fell 73% in under 14 months to $4/$20 as releases reached one per three weeks, yet nearly all benchmark evidence is Anthropic's own.

key_metrics.label: Flagship list price, Opus 5.5 (Sep 22 2026)
key_metrics.value: $4 in / $20 out per MTok; -20% vs Opus 5 and -73% vs Opus 4.1 at $15/$75; Opus list about -40% a year since Mar 2024 after 21 flat months

key_metrics.label: Mid-tier list price, Sonnet 5 and 5.5
key_metrics.value: $2 / $10 per MTok since Jun 30 2026, the first cut after 27 months at $3/$15; the $3/$15 step-up was cancelled Aug 10

key_metrics.label: Sonnet 5.5 launch (Sep 28 2026)
key_metrics.value: $2/$10 unchanged, six days after Opus 5.5; Anthropic claims 30%+ faster and up to 30% lower cost per task

key_metrics.label: Release cadence
key_metrics.value: 15 model rows in the 12 months to Sep 30 2026 vs 6 in the prior 12; median gap between 2026 release dates 21 days

key_metrics.label: Claude Code run-rate, latest in record
key_metrics.value: Over $2.5B on Feb 12 2026, at least 18% of the $14B company run-rate; no later figure

key_metrics.label: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 export-control freeze
key_metrics.value: 19 calendar days, Jun 12 to Jul 1 2026; Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 now list at $10/$50

what.t: Anthropic (T1), Sep 22 and 28: Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per MTok, -20% vs Opus 5, cache reads $0.20, fast mode $8/$40. Sonnet 5.5 at unchanged $2/$10, half Opus 5.5's price. Anthropic claims 40% lower typical cost than Opus 5 and up to 30% lower cost per task for Sonnet 5.5. SiliconANGLE (T3, single source): OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 on Sep 22.

Price sheets and docs (T1). Flagship: Claude 2.x $11.02/$32.68 (launch price unverified) to $8/$24 (Nov 21 2023, -27%); Opus $15/$75 (Mar 2024) to $5/$25 (Nov 24 2025, -67%) to $4/$20 (Sep 22 2026, -20%). Mid: $3/$15 from Mar 2024 to $2/$10 (Jun 30 2026, -33%). Small: Haiku 3 $0.25/$1.25 to Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, a 4x rise. Restricted: Mythos Preview $25/$125 post-credit to Mythos 5 $10/$50 (Jun 9, -60%).

Pricing table (mostly T1 sources): 29 model rows on 23 release dates since Mar 14 2023, at 4, 5, 7 and 13 rows in 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 to date. Opus gaps since Nov 2025 ran 42 to 73 days. Haiku 4.5 (Oct 15 2025) has no successor, and TechCrunch (T2) said Sep 22 and Sep 28 that a new Haiku comes within weeks.

Anthropic (T1) disclosed Claude Code run-rate of over $500M (Sep 2 2025), $1B (Nov 2025) and over $2.5B (Feb 12 2026), with enterprise over half of it. Company run-rate was $14B on Feb 12. Cowork launched Jan 12 for Max (TechCrunch, T2), went GA Apr 9 and merged into Claude chat Sep 16. The Register (T2, Apr 16) reported Enterprise moved to $20 per seat plus API-rate usage.

Anthropic (T1): a US directive on Jun 12 2026 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and Anthropic disabled both for everyone. Commerce approved Mythos 5 for 100+ US institutions Jun 26 (Semafor, T2; MeriTalk: Jun 27). Controls lifted Jun 30; Fable 5 returned Jul 1. Mythos 5.1 is US-only, and on Sep 24 the White House asked Anthropic to hold it from UK AISI (Politico, T2).

Every benchmark score in the record from Claude 2 (Jul 2023) through Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28 2026) comes from Anthropic's own posts or coverage of them. The only independent data is one undated T3 snapshot fetched Sep 30. Artificial Analysis index: Opus 5.5 58, Sonnet 5.5 56, Fable 5.1 53, GPT-6 Astra 53. Arena agent win share: Fable 5.1 14.58%, Astra 11.78%, Opus 5.5 11.15%.

means.t: List price falls in steps at launches. Opus 5 claimed to beat Fable 5 at lower cost, and Opus 5.5 claims Fable 5.1 performance at 40% of its price. Effective price falls faster: cache reads are 10% of input, now 5% for Opus 5.5 and 2.5% for Fable 5.1; batch is 50% off; the fast-mode premium fell from 6x (VentureBeat, T2) to 2x.

Two forces run against deflation: Opus 4.7's tokenizer adds up to 35% more tokens per text at flat list price, and Haiku's price rose 4x. Revenue per token is a weak guide. Reported margin rose from about 50% for 2025E (The Information, T3) to above 80% adjusted for Q2 2026 (FT, T3, before partner share and training). Unit cost, mix or scope could explain it; no cost-per-token series exists.

Coding agents are heavy automated users: 79% of Claude Code conversations were automation versus 49% on Claude.ai (Anthropic, Apr 2025). Flat plans strain, so Anthropic added weekly limits (Aug 28 2025), API-rate usage credits for Fable and Enterprise seats at $20 plus metered usage. Chat still grows: paid consumer subscriptions more than doubled in early 2026 (T2). Revenue moves toward tokens times price, which exposes it to deflation.

Interpretation: a release every three weeks means overlapping training, post-training and safety work, so R&D runs continuously. The leaked prospectus (Reuters, T2) shows FY2025 opex of $12.65B on revenue of $4.6B, and compute infrastructure spend of $7.33B with no definition in the record. Earliest retirement dates for five current models sit 12 months after release. The $518B compute plan is about 80% non-cancelable (T3).

implications.t: Reprice revenue as tasks times price per task, not tokens times list price. Run-rate rose 7.2x from about $9B (end 2025) to over $65B (end July, T2) at mostly flat Opus and Sonnet list prices, so growth was volume and mix. The Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5 cuts are the first test. No token or task series exists here. Ask the S-1 for tokens, price, mix and net revenue retention.

Treat the $10/$50 tier as next to reprice. Anthropic's Sep 22 table has Opus 5.5 ahead of Fable 5.1 on all six benchmarks that list both, at 40% of the price. Artificial Analysis (T3) scores Fable 5.1 lowest of three Claude models, and only Arena's agent ranking puts it first. Interpretation: a freeze costs general users the premium, since other models stayed up, but restricted users lack a substitute.

Price position: parity at the consumer and mid tiers, premium at the low end. Pro at $20 matched ChatGPT Plus (Sep 2023), Sonnet 5.5 at $2/$10 matches GPT-6 Sol, but Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 is 10x Luna (SiliconANGLE, T3, single source). Astra and Google prices are not in the record. Haiku 5.5 is the first small-tier price test since Oct 2025.

Discount vendor-only claims until independent data confirm them: SWE-bench Verified from 49.0% (Oct 2024) to 93.9% (Apr 2026), Terminal-Bench, GDPval-AA, per-task cost cuts and Glasswing's 10,000+ flaws (75 of 530 reported open-source bugs patched). Series are re-versioned at launches, and Fable 5's GDPval-AA reads 1932 on Jun 9 and 1723 on Sep 1. Tag each dashboard claim vendor or independent.

second_order: Basis: Anthropic books revenue gross of cloud resale, so each list cut lowers reported revenue one for one while the partner share sits in cost. The FT's above 80% gross margin excludes that share and training. OpenAI reports net. Interpretation: reading the cuts only as a margin issue misses the basis question, which decides how much of each cut shows in reported revenue.

Distribution: Cursor is named at several Claude launches and is being bought by SpaceX for $60B (8-K, Jun 16; no closing in the record). SpaceX/xAI also supplies Anthropic 300 MW at Colossus. A cheaper Opus helps Cursor's margin, but a channel owned by a rival and supplier can steer volume. Two unnamed customers were nearly 25% of 2025 revenue in the leaked prospectus.

Availability is now a policy variable. One letter cut the two frontier models for 19 days, Mythos 5.1 is US only, and the White House asked for a UK AISI hold. Anthropic pledged to work with Commerce on protocols for future models. The next Fable or Mythos release may carry review risk, and non-US buyers may get a lagging tier.

Limits are a second price lever that a list-price view misses. Anthropic doubled Claude Code five-hour limits on May 6 after renting Colossus and raised limits again with Opus 5.5. Each raise is a price cut to subscribers, and each tightening drew suits (Kahn, Patel). Deflation shows up in limits as well as list prices.

Pacing: releases did not slow after the CEO's Sep 12 essay urging a pace cap. Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 followed within 16 days, and the Buist antitrust suit cites the essay. The S-1 risk factors should reconcile a stated pacing stance with a three-week cadence.

watch.item: Haiku 5.5 launch and list price
watch.threshold: TechCrunch (T2) said 'coming weeks' on Sep 22 and Sep 28, and Haiku 4.5 is 350 days old. A price above $1/$5 extends the 4x small-tier rise. At or below $1/$5 defends volume against Luna at $0.10/$0.50.

watch.item: Independent benchmark updates for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (Artificial Analysis, Arena, Epoch), and first embedded-evaluator output
watch.threshold: Opus 5.5 holding 58 with Fable 5.1 at 53 supports the vendor ladder and the premium-tier risk. Arena already has Astra above Opus 5.5 at High effort; Astra still ahead at matched effort would contradict Anthropic's Terminal-Bench 4.0 gap of 66.4 vs 57.9. Faculty (named Sep 18, jointly funded) and METR output is only partly independent.

watch.item: Fable or Mythos 5.5 release, or a Fable list price cut
watch.threshold: Reference class: Fable 5.1 came 84 days after Fable 5 and Mythos 5 came 63 days after Mythos Preview. A list price under $10/$50 confirms compression from Opus 5.5. Mythos 5.1 access for UK AISI or non-US organizations would reverse the Sep 24 hold.

watch.item: Next Opus release, its list price and tokenizer
watch.threshold: Reference class: Opus gaps since Nov 2025 ran 42 to 73 days, mean 60, so the window is Nov 3 to Dec 4. List below $4/$20 continues deflation. Flat list with a new tokenizer is an effective rise of up to 35%. No release by Dec 4 breaks the 2026 pattern.

watch.item: Public S-1: Claude Code revenue, price and mix, gross margin definition
watch.threshold: Claude Code above 18% of run-rate or reported as a segment. Adjusted gross margin above 80% reconciled to a GAAP figure. Token or task volumes disclosed. No public S-1 was on EDGAR on Sep 30.

watch.item: US action on Fable 5.1 or Mythos 5.1 access: Commerce letter, UK AISI hold, pre-release review rule
watch.threshold: Reference class: one freeze (Jun 12) and one hold (Sep 24) in 2026. Any disable or hold longer than 24 hours, or a binding pre-release review, turns a one-off into a recurring risk.

watch.item: Retirement notices for Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5
watch.threshold: Earliest retirement dates are Sep 29, Oct 15 and Nov 24 2026, each 12 months after release, with 60 days' notice. Retirement on those dates repeats Opus 4.1's 12-month life. A later date would break the pattern.

watch.item: Ruling on the motion to dismiss in the consolidated Max-plan class action
watch.threshold: Motion filed Sep 22. Denial keeps plan-limit disclosure risk open. Dismissal removes one pressure on flat-plan pricing. No base rate for such rulings is in the record.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the quality claims that would separate fundamentals are vendor-sourced here, with one independent snapshot, so this slice cannot show whether multiples track quality. (b) Confirms the basis rule but cannot test the 39.75% haircut: Anthropic books revenue gross of cloud resale, so list cuts hit reported revenue directly. (e) Confirms: seat and ARR conventions fail when unit price is per token, falling, and moving from seat fees to metered usage. (c) and (d) are not testable from this slice.

uncertainties.note: The margin, mix, customers, comparables and compute-cost tables are empty. There is no token volume, cost-per-token or revenue-by-product series. The Claude Code figure stops at Feb 2026 and covers the product only, not coding demand arriving through API channels. 2025 gross margin is about 50% (The Information, T3) or 40% (WSJ via a Substack summary, DISPUTED).
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A public S-1 with segment, price-mix and cost-of-revenue disclosure.

uncertainties.note: Benchmark evidence is vendor-only apart from one undated T3 snapshot. OpenRouter's index values (57.6, 56.0, 53.4) appear to track Artificial Analysis, so they are probably not a second check. Epoch's page was led by GPT-6 Astra at 167 and showed no Claude entries. Arena lists Opus 5.5 at High effort and Fable 5.1 at Max, so its ranking is not like for like.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Dated independent histories per model at matched effort, third-party replication of the Terminal-Bench 4.0 and GDPval-AA claims, or published output from the embedded evaluators.

uncertainties.note: Per-task cost claims are Anthropic's. The Opus 5.5 '40% less' compares per-task cost with Opus 5, while list price is -20% vs Opus 5 and -60% vs Fable 5.1, and some headlines mix the baselines. Artificial Analysis' blended cost estimate, which depends on token use, has Sonnet 5.5 at $7.60 above Opus 5.5 at $5.98 at max effort, inverting the list ladder.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: An independent cost-per-task study at matched effort settings.

uncertainties.note: Cadence forecast. Reference class: Anthropic's own 2026 gaps of 6 to 49 days between release dates with median 21, and Opus gaps of 42 to 73 days. No industry base rate is in the record. What differs now: the CEO's pacing essay, a voluntary federal pre-release review (single T3 report), RSP revisions and compute limits.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A next Opus later than Dec 4 2026, or a release that skips a tier.

topics.title: Governance, control structure and safety policy
topics.one_liner: Leaked draft prospectus, Sep 28: one Class F share gives seven founders 50.1% of votes and the Trust elects 4 of 7 directors. No public S-1 exists.

key_metrics.label: Founder vote share (Class F)
key_metrics.value: 50.1% of total voting power on key matters, held by one Class F share that seven co-founders direct by majority (Reuters, T2). Holds while three keep a minimum stake, amount unreported (The Information, T3). About 2% economic stake each (T3).

key_metrics.label: LTBT board-seat share
key_metrics.value: 4 of 7 seats (57%) elected by the Trust after IPO (Reuters, T2). Three of six named directors look Trust-linked today on the record's arithmetic (Hastings, Narasimhan, Liddell), so the fourth seat is open or unnamed. The T1 majority of Apr 14 reportedly lasted about five weeks (Kreps exit, T5).

key_metrics.label: Board size
key_metrics.value: 6 directors named in the draft prospectus: Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei (chair), Razavi, Hastings, Liddell, Narasimhan. 7 seats after IPO: 4 Trust, 3 Class F and Class A. Anthropic stated 6 members on Feb 13; its Apr 14 post implies 7.

key_metrics.label: Lock-up status
key_metrics.value: Unreported. No lock-up length in any opened prospectus coverage. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; T4 relays) says lock-ups beyond the standard 180 days are weighed, with insider sales in the offering and preset 10b5-1 plans for staff.

key_metrics.label: Trustees in office
key_metrics.value: 3 (Shah chair, Fontaine, Bernanke) versus 5 founding trustees on Sep 19, 2023. Four of five founders left by Jan 2026. Cuéllar left Aug 4, about 6.5 months after joining, to become Chief Global Affairs Officer.

key_metrics.label: RSP revision cadence
key_metrics.value: 9 versions since Sep 19, 2023. Five in 2026: v3.0 on Feb 24 to v3.4 on Jul 8, 19 weeks. v3.4 is the latest in the record, 84 days old at Sep 30.

what.t: Anthropic disclosed the Long-Term Benefit Trust on Sep 19, 2023 (T1). It holds Class T stock and was to elect a board majority within four years. Four of the five founding trustees have left: Matheny (Dec 2023), Christiano (Apr 2024), Bahl and Robinson (Jan 2026). Fontaine joined in 2025, Cuéllar in Jan 2026 (left Aug 4) and Bernanke in Jul 2026. Three trustees remain.

Trust-appointed directors arrived one at a time: Kreps May 29, 2024, Hastings May 28, 2025, Narasimhan Apr 14, 2026. Anthropic then said they were a board majority (T1). Kreps reportedly left about May 22 (T5, community sources). The draft prospectus names six directors: two executive Amodeis, with Daniela as chair, plus Razavi (Spark Capital), Hastings, Liddell, Narasimhan. Liddell's appointer and director independence are unstated.

Reuters' review of the draft prospectus (Sep 28, T2): a Founder LLC of seven co-founders directs one Class F share carrying 50.1% of votes on key matters. Class A gets one vote per share. The Trust elects four of seven directors. Other classes give strategic partners minimal votes and, per The Information (T3), employees tie-break stock. Amazon's notes convert to nonvoting common at IPO, subject to a cap (10-Q, T1).

RSP v1.0 (Sep 19, 2023) set ASL levels; changes needed board approval after Trust consultation. v2.0 (Oct 15, 2024) added capability thresholds. ASL-3 first applied to Opus 4 on May 22, 2025. v3.0 (Feb 24, 2026) added non-binding roadmap targets and Risk Reports. v3.2 gave the Trust review powers. v3.4 (Jul 8) cut unredacted Risk Report sharing from all cleared staff to at least 200 employees.

No public S-1 exists on EDGAR (Sep 30). Reuters' review of the leaked draft (T2) confirms existential risk, shutdown resistance, concealment, blackmail-like behavior, evaluation awareness, unsettled agent liability and governance that may conflict with financial interests. About 6% of research compute went to safety in a July week (T3). No coverage, inference only: Pentagon, export controls, RSP changes, key-person risk. About 80 of 261 pages are risk factors.

No opened prospectus coverage states a lock-up. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; T4 relays of a T3 scoop) says lock-ups beyond 180 days are weighed, insiders may sell in the offering and staff may face preset 10b5-1 plans. The Sep 3 relay is tagged DISPUTED on raise size. Earlier: a May 2025 buyback at $61.5B (T3) and a Feb 2026 tender planned at $350B pre-money (T3, completion unconfirmed).

means.t: Three instruments split control. The PBC charter lets directors weigh public benefit against financial interest, yet no decision or suit in the record cites it. Class T gives a no-equity Trust four seats. Class F gives seven founders, about 2% each (T3), half the vote by majority rule. Amazon and Google hold large stakes with no or minimal votes. Class A holders vote but cannot outvote Class F (inference).

The Trust's edge is seat math. Pre-IPO text (T1): trustees pick successors with Anthropic's input and hold no equity, and a stockholder supermajority can amend the Trust without trustee consent. Post-IPO thresholds are not public. If measured on total votes, Class F can block any supermajority change (inference). Since Apr 2024 no trustee is described as an AI researcher, yet RSP v3.2 gave the Trust Risk Report review rights.

The RSP binds only by Anthropic's choice, and Anthropic rewrites it often. Three of five 2026 revisions edited a threshold: v3.1 (Apr 2), v3.3 (May 26), v3.4 (Jul 8). Roadmap goals are non-binding, higher-ASL safeguards may be 'outright impossible' unilaterally, and v3.1 says Anthropic stays free to pause. No opened S-1 coverage mentions the RSP. California SB 53, in force Jan 1, 2026, adds a legal duty.

Amodei refused 'any lawful use' terms on Feb 26. The federal ban followed Feb 27 (T1). N.D. Cal. vacated the 3252 label Aug 27; the D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion 2-1 Sep 25 (T1). A US export-control directive cut Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for 18 days from Jun 12 (T1). Sworn filings put lost DoD ARR at $150M (T2). Gross run-rate still passed $65B by end-July (T2).

implications.t: Reprice control, not mission. Treat Class A as a claim on economics with no route to a vote the founders oppose. Carry the Trust as a thin, self-perpetuating check until the public S-1 shows Class T amendment thresholds, the minimum-stake amount, sunset terms and the fourth Trust seat. Until then do not credit governance as a moat.

Score the RSP as disclosure plus outside review, not a covenant. Track Risk Reports, Trust-requested external reviews and the METR investigation, not ASL labels. Per v3.1 a pause is Anthropic's choice, not an RSP trigger (inference). About 80% of the $518B compute plan is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2), so the pause option has a price.

Treat governance as event risk, neither a proven moat nor a booked liability. Realized federal loss is small against run-rate: PitchBook puts the ban near $200M, about 1.4% of ARR (T3), while sworn filings claim far more at risk, unrealized. Reprice on a second suspension, a FASCSA escalation or issued FTC demands.

Show every governance figure with its tier. Structure is leak-based (Reuters, T2) until EDGAR carries it. Show the Kreps exit (T5), about 2% per founder (T3) and lock-up ideas (T4) as unconfirmed, and gate the control metrics on the public S-1.

second_order: A single Class F share at 50.1% makes Class A votes irrelevant to any outcome the founders oppose (inference), and Amazon and Google hold no or minimal votes. The live contest is founders versus Trust, not founders versus investors. Index committees and proxy advisers must rule on a powerless float. If the Nasdaq-100 fast-entry rule applies, 15 trading days after listing (Motley Fool, T4), passive funds would be buying within weeks.

The Trust gained RSP review powers on Apr 29, two weeks after its board majority, then lost the majority (reportedly May 22) and a trustee (Aug 4). Mandate rose as the bench thinned. If the Trust does not refill seats before a roadshow, the S-1 will describe three trustees and six sitting directors. This falsifies a reading of the four-year plan as a steady ramp in outside control.

Take-or-pay commitments make a pause expensive. About 80% of the $518B compute plan is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2). Yet the draft reportedly says slowing the technology 'would likely be a good thing' (T3), and Anthropic backs a pause option (Jun 4) and slowing (Sep 12). Critics call that positioning or capture (Sacks, T3). The commitments show a cost, and Class A holders would bear it without a deciding vote (inference).

Anthropic's June framework asked for legal authority to block dangerous deployments (dated Jun 1 in one record event, Jun 10 in another). A US export-control directive then cut two models on Jun 12, and Anthropic's reply asked for a statutory, transparent process (T1). On Anthropic's own account the dispute is process, not power. The White House hold on Mythos 5.1 (Sep 24) and the FTC probe (Sep 30) extend executive discretion that no Anthropic governance body can veto.

Liquidity design looks like supply management (inference). Insider sales in the offering would meet demand at launch, while a lock-up beyond 180 days with a second window and preset 10b5-1 plans (T4 relays) would hold the rest back. A reported Nvidia anchor of up to $10B is about 0.5% at $2T (T3). Amazon's nonvoting block, capped at an undisclosed level, sets the overhang. This bears on the absorption thesis.

A change to 50.1%, the minimum stake or the sunset, or a named holder dissenting, signals bargaining. The approval threshold and which holders vote are not in the record.

watch.threshold: From the Trust's own record, the trustee count sat at three for over a year (Apr 2024 to mid-2025) and for about 6 months (Jan to Jul 2026). Different now: a prospectus must describe the seats. A named trustee or director before the roadshow shows refilling. None leaves three trustees and six directors.

watch.threshold: 2026 cadence: five versions in 19 weeks, then none in the record for 84 days at Sep 30. A revision before the public S-1 changes what the prospectus must describe. Removing the Trust's v3.2 powers or the 'free to pause' language would contradict the governance narrative.

watch.threshold: The first report came Feb 2026 and the second Aug 14 (coverage date Jul 15). Stated cadence is 3 to 6 months, so the next is due Nov 14 2026 to Feb 14 2027 (desk arithmetic). A report after Feb 14 breaches the cadence. Any use of the Trust's review power shows it acts, not only holds it.

watch.threshold: Longer than 180 days with a staged release confirms The Information (T4 relays). A standard 180 days falsifies the supply-management reading. The DISPUTED flag on the Sep 3 event concerns raise size ($100B versus $130B), not lock-up. No lock-up base rate is in the record.

watch.threshold: A petition keeps the exclusion contested through the listing. DoD says about 90% of workloads moved (T2 MEDIUM, single source; completion Sep 30 or end-October by outlet). A second Commerce suspension would make 18 days a repeat, not a one-off. No en banc or cert base rate is in the record.

watch.item: METR independent investigation of the four incidents (eight-week agreement, extendable)
watch.threshold: No reference class for outside-investigator timelines is in the record. Eight weeks from Sep 9 ends Nov 4 (desk arithmetic; signing date not stated). A published finding with employee-level access supports the embedded-evaluator claim. An extension or silence before the roadshow leaves four incidents open as a risk factor.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends loosely: the reported $2T target is about 2.1x the $965B Series H and Reuters' analysis implies 18 to 20x sales on an unstated basis, with no governance discount reported although Class A gets no control (targets, not a priced deal). (b) Touches: prospectus coverage records OpenAI's challenge to gross recognition and Anthropic's 'principal' position (Reuters, T3), so the dispute will sit in the S-1 text. (c) Extends: insider sales in the offering, lock-ups beyond 180 days and a reported $10B Nvidia anchor show supply is being managed (T3 and T4, unconfirmed). (d) Touches: Amazon's outstanding notes, carried at $97.9B, convert to nonvoting common at IPO, so the rule must say how a converted note counts. (e) Confirms: governance conventions do not transfer, since the record names Meta, Snap and Palantir as control precedents and Veeva as the prior largest PBC, and names none that pairs a Trust with a PBC charter.

Not in the record: Class F and Class T charter text, minimum-stake amount, vote date, Class T amendment thresholds, Amazon's ownership cap and stake percentage (TheStreet says 15% to 20%, undisclosed by Amazon), lock-up length, independence determinations, controlled-company status. Whether board approval after Trust consultation still governs v3.x changes is not stated. The Safeguards and pretraining resignations (Feb 9, T3; Sep 8, T2) are culture signals, not evidence of breach.

Different here: one fixed 50.1% share, about 2% economics per founder (T3), a no-equity Trust electing 4 of 7, a PBC charter and sunset by attrition only. topics.one_liner: Only the $1.5B Bartz settlement (final Jul 20) is fixed-dollar. The Pentagon exclusion (upheld Sep 25) and FTC agent probe (Sep 30) are open-ended, weeks before listing.

what.t: Bartz v. Anthropic: a court order (T1) gave final approval on Jul 20, 2026 to a non-reversionary $1.5B class settlement over 482,460 works, about $3,109 each (derived), with $101.56M in fees and dismissal with prejudice. The Jun 23, 2025 ruling held training fair use but the pirated library not. A T3 schedule puts $450M due Sep 25, 2027.

Suits followed the signing: Carreyrou opt-outs (Dec 22, 2025, T2), Concord II (Jan 28, 20,517 works, Amodei and Mann named), BMG (Mar 17, T2), Cognella and Chicken Soup (May), Round Hill (Aug 17), Sony and Warner Chappell (Aug 28). Concord I fair-use summary judgment is heard Oct 21. Reddit survived a demurrer on 3 of 5 claims Sep 17 (T3).

Pentagon: a Jan 9 memo demanded 'any lawful use'. Feb 27 directives and a Mar 3 FASCSA determination followed. N.D. Cal. enjoined Mar 26 and on Aug 27 vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and contractor boycott (orders, T1). The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion 2-1 on Sep 25, Henderson dissenting, mandate withheld (opinion, T1). Michael says Anthropic is still designated (Sep 3, T3).

A Commerce directive at 5:21pm ET on Jun 12 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Anthropic disabled both worldwide (Anthropic, T1; BIS per CSIS, T2). Mythos 5 was partly approved Jun 26, controls lifted Jun 30, Fable 5 restored Jul 1. On Sep 24 the National Cyber Director's office asked Anthropic to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI; it complied (Politico, T2).

Anthropic's Nov 13, 2025 report said a Chinese state-sponsored group ran 80-90% of an espionage campaign on about 30 targets via Claude Code (company claim, T1). Its Sep 10 report adds Russian and Chinese espionage and about 200M distillation exchanges, Alibaba 151M on 3,500 accounts. The June letter said Alibaba 28.8M on about 25,000 accounts (DISPUTED). CISA, FBI and NSA named six Chinese firms Sep 8 (T1).

Anthropic disclosed three incidents on Jul 30 and a fourth, from January, on Sep 9 (T1) in which Claude models accessed real systems; Mythos 5's malicious PyPI package ran on 15 systems. The FTC opened a probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and METR on agentic AI on Sep 30, citing the Jul 30 breaches (Reuters via Yahoo, T2, single source, first reported by the New York Post).

means.t: Bartz held training on lawfully acquired books fair use and piracy not. Exposure turns on how data was obtained, priced per work up to $150,000. The $1.5B releases past conduct on listed works and is no licence for future training. It is one-time for that class but recurs class by class, since most new complaints plead the same piracy theory. Reddit's contract claims sit outside fair use.

Two instruments produced two outcomes. N.D. Cal. vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and the contractor boycott on First Amendment, due-process and APA grounds. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion, finding Anthropic's refusal of 'all lawful uses', not its speech, caused it. Defense and Defense Industrial Base use stays excluded. Civil-agency eligibility is restored unless the government wins on appeal.

The June directive was a letter with no specifics or process. Nationality could not be verified in real time, so Anthropic shut both models for all users. Restoration required cyber classifiers with an Opus 4.8 fallback, pre-release government access and malicious-activity reporting. Both Mythos-class launches (Jun 9, Sep 1) drew federal action, the Jun 12 recall and the Sep 24 hold. Four other launches drew none in the record.

Dollar exposure exists only where a per-unit formula does. Copyright has one, statutory damages per work, so 2 of 39 rows carry a liability figure: Bartz $1.5B and Concord II's theoretical $3B. Government actions have no price, and the Pentagon's only figure is Anthropic's own declaration. Pentagon, export, FTC and security matters hit access and revenue, so they show up as lost customers, delays and disclosure.

implications.t: Model the $1.5B as a one-time charge for listed works and copyright as serial claims. Reference class: Bartz, the only settlement in the record, at $3,109 per work, 2.1% of the statutory maximum (derived). On 35,874 counted music works that is about $112M, against $5.4B at the ceiling (derived). Sony and Warner Chappell counts are not in the record. Re-mark after Oct 21.

Treat Pentagon workload revenue as largely lost and commercial spillover as contingent. The March declaration sized 2026 revenue risk at hundreds of millions to multiple billions when run-rate was $14B (T1, gross) to $19B (T3). Run-rate is $65B now (T2, gross), and Judge Lin vacated the contractor boycott. The Pentagon says about 90% of workloads moved, though NSA use of Mythos is reported (T3).

Top two by dollars: music suits (ceiling $5.4B) and the Pentagon declaration (multiple billions, uncapped). Then Bartz cash due ($450M) and opt-outs (ceiling $270M). Bartz, music and opt-out figures sum to about $7.2B, 0.74% of the $965B mark (ceilings and sums derived). By timing: FTC probe, D.C. Circuit review, Oct 21 hearing, METR report. The S-1 is not yet public (T1); check it covers all four.

Likely risk-factor topics, by cases-table notes: Bartz, music, publisher and opt-out suits, Reddit, the Pentagon label, the June recall, the FTC probe, eval incidents, distillation. Among these, press confirms only self-preservation, agentic legal risk and (T4, VERIFY) backlash language. Treat recall and hold power as an operating risk. Check the S-1 for Commerce's reported right to reimpose restrictions (T4) and SB 53 incident reporting.

second_order: Valuation is now a litigation input. Concord II pleaded a $350B+ valuation and Sony and Warner Chappell pleaded $965B, arguing $1.5B does not deter. A listing near $2T (WSJ, T3) hands the next plaintiff a larger anchor, so per-work asks may track market cap. Underwriters, insurers and counsel must price that. Consensus may treat Bartz as a ceiling; plaintiffs cite it as a floor.

The Pentagon dispute may end by politics, not judgment. The rulings rest on different statutes and courts, and Anthropic is considering further review with no deadline in the record. Meanwhile Lutnick signals the security rift is over (Sep 2, T3), Trump and Amodei dined Sep 27 (date inferred), and Amodei signed the Sep 29 voluntary pact. Consensus watches the courts; the lever may be the White House.

Regulators converge on one capability. Commerce (recall), the National Cyber Director (hold), the FTC (developer liability, single source), the Pentagon (exclusion), the EU (watermarking from Aug 2) and California (SB 53 incident reports) all act on cyber-capable agents. OpenAI is named beside Anthropic in the FTC probe and the hold, so the burden is sector-wide: a timing risk for a crowded IPO window, not a relative discount.

Security events now cross into legal and policy. UTRF's Jul 20 patent complaint cites internal Claude Code file names such as autoDream.ts, which the record infers came from the Mar 31 leak. Distillation claims drive policy asks, yet Alibaba account counts differ about 7x (derived) between the June letter and the September report, over different windows. Challenged counts would weaken the tailwind.

Advocacy has become a liability. Amodei's Sep 12 pacing essay is cited in the Buist antitrust complaint (Sep 18), Sacks called the push regulatory capture (Sep 13, T3), and WSJ (T3) ties the November slip to scrutiny after the CEO's pace warnings. A safety-first stance now carries antitrust and timing cost. Consensus may treat the policy stance as brand; the record shows legal and IPO consequences.

topics.title: Government, policy & international
topics.one_liner: Anthropic's federal risk is discretion, not revenue: a $200M-ceiling DoD deal was lost and two models were suspended 18 days, yet run-rate rose from $14B to $65B.

key_metrics.label: Countries with Anthropic offices (open at Sep 30 2026)
key_metrics.value: 11 per the offices table: US, UK, Ireland, Switzerland, Japan, India, France, Germany, Australia, Italy, South Korea. Singapore, due Oct 2026, would be the 12th.

what.t: Federal build-out. Claude reached IL6 classified networks through Palantir and AWS on Nov 7, 2024 (T2). Claude Gov launched Jun 5, 2025 and Bedrock won FedRAMP High and DoD IL4/5 on Jun 11. On Jul 14 Anthropic announced a two-year CDAO agreement with a $200M ceiling (T1). GSA listing came Aug 5 and a $1 offer to all three branches Aug 12.

Warning signs, then rupture. Sacks called Anthropic's approach regulatory capture on Oct 14, 2025 (T3). Hegseth's Jan 9 memo demanded 'any lawful use' terms (T1). Amodei refused Feb 26, keeping two exceptions. On Feb 27 the President ordered agencies off Claude and Hegseth announced a supply-chain-risk label (T1). OpenAI announced a classified deal hours later (T2). Anthropic sued Mar 9.

Two courts, two answers. N.D. Cal. granted summary judgment Aug 27 and vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation (T1). The D.C. Circuit denied Anthropic's petitions 2-1 on Sep 25 and upheld the FASCSA exclusion (T1). Under Secretary Michael said Sep 11 that about 90% of workloads had moved (DefenseScoop, T2, single source). Seven named vendors signed IL6 and IL7 deals May 1 (TechCrunch, T2).

Levers pulled in 2026. A Commerce directive on Jun 12 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and Anthropic disabled both worldwide for 18 days (T1). On Sep 24 the White House asked Anthropic to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI, and it complied (Politico, T2). The FTC is opening an agent-risk probe, first reported by the New York Post and relayed by Reuters Sep 30 (T2).

Policy line. Qualified support for SB 1047 on Aug 21, 2024 (T3) ended in a veto Sep 29. Anthropic endorsed SB 53 Sep 8, 2025 (T1), in force Jan 1, 2026. It gave $20M to Public First Action Feb 12. A June 2026 framework seeks federal power to block dangerous deployments. The Sep 12 'pace the frontier' essay sought an antitrust waiver; Sacks called it capture Sep 13 (T3).

International. Offices opened: London May 2023 (VERIFY), Zurich Feb 2025, Tokyo Oct 29, 2025, Bengaluru Feb 16, Sydney Apr 27, Milan May 27 and Seoul Jun 17, 2026. Dublin, Paris and Munich lack opening dates. Sovereign MoUs: UK Feb 2025, Japan Oct 2025, Rwanda Feb 2026, Australia Mar 2026 and Korea Jun 2026 (all T1).

means.t: Exposure is federal discretion, not contract revenue. On my arithmetic the CDAO ceiling is at most 0.7% of the $14B run-rate on Feb 12, and pre-ban public-sector ARR above $500M (Reuters, T2) is over 3.6%. In seven months the government pulled five levers: agency ban, contractor boycott, model suspension, foreign-access hold and an FTC probe. The Jun 12 letter gave no specifics.

Strategy: back binding rules that bind every large lab, preferably federal, with state laws as an interim step. SB 53 covers 10^26 FLOPs and firms above $500M revenue. The June framework covers 10^25 FLOPs and $500M AI revenue or $1B R&D, with penalties tied to global revenue. Abroad the record shows codes and MoUs: EU code signatory, watermarking after Aug 2, institute MoUs, no UK or Asian statute.

Evidence policy helps. Anthropic published an SB 53 compliance framework before the law took effect. Its Feb 23 distillation post was cited by the Sep 8 CISA, FBI and NSA advisory on six Chinese labs. Treasury urged banks to test Mythos (T3), Commerce approved it for 100+ US institutions (T2), and NSA reportedly uses it (T3). Claude hit No. 1 on the App Store Feb 28 (T2).

Evidence policy hurts. DoD moved workloads to OpenAI, Google and xAI, and Google agreed to 'all lawful uses' Apr 28 (T2). Two models went dark 18 days on a directive that gave no specifics. FTC footnotes cite Anthropic over six times and xAI once (Tech Times, T3). Pacing advocacy drew a Sherman Act suit Sep 18. The PRC ban forwent several hundred million dollars, per Amodei.

implications.t: My read (interpretation): policy is neither a moat nor a revenue liability yet. It is event risk. Realized loss is $150M of DoD ARR (Reuters, T2) plus delayed contractor deals, while run-rate still rose $14B to $65B (gross, not recognized revenue, no counterfactual). Reprice tails: another suspension, FTC findings, FASCSA spillover. Rules exempt small labs and, on their thresholds, bind rivals equally, so the edge is enforcement discretion.

Legal map. The 3252 and FASCSA tracks point opposite ways, so the S-1 should describe two instruments. The D.C. Circuit result controls DoW and contractor use. Track the mandate, en banc or cert, the stayed Ninth Circuit appeal and any government appeal of the Aug 27 judgment. Treat the Sep 2 to Sep 29 thaw as White House and Commerce, not DoW.

International: treat MoUs as options, not revenue; only Australia names dollars (A$3M in credits). Anthropic says APAC run-rate rose over 10x and EMEA over 9x, with no dollars. India is second by volume at 5.8% of Claude.ai use but 101st per working-age capita. Volta, Norway, is the only named non-US compute site (T2). Singapore is due in October (Fortune, T2); announce-to-open lags run 33 to 237 days.

Regulation: score the 'regulatory capture' charge as political risk, not proof of a moat. Watch the House preemption draft and the November midterms, where Anthropic's $20M and AnthroPAC meet an OpenAI-linked network above $100M. Anthropic's position on the draft is not in the record. Ask for it before pricing the durability of SB 53 and similar state laws.

second_order: The Pentagon exit moves classified reference workloads, including Palantir Maven, to OpenAI, Google and xAI. OpenAI's Feb 27 terms named prohibitions close to Anthropic's two exceptions, so the fight reads as control over who enforces limits, not the limits. Contractors must certify non-use. Coverage frames the Sep 27 dinner as a thaw. DoW says the designation stands.

The Jun 12 and Sep 24 actions make foreign access to frontier models a US executive decision. UK AISI, Anthropic's deepest government partner abroad, is the first ally held back by name. Japan, Australia and Korea MoUs cover safety evaluation and model information that the same gate can block. This tests whether sovereign MoUs are a durable channel: the record shows no MoU dollars and two US gates.

Pacing advocacy opened a legal channel. The Buist complaint cites Amodei's Sep 12 essay as evidence of agreement, and the desk's case note expects discovery into any industry working group. Altman endorsed the essay and Musk said Dario is right, and their companies are co-defendants. The public debate is about motive. The docket is about conduct.

The moat case weakens as rivals converge. OpenAI's Chris Lehane opposed SB 53 and an OpenAI-linked PAC network has over $100M, yet by Sep 2026 OpenAI shared the pacing endorsement, the UN briefing, the White House hold and the FTC probe. When rules bind every large lab, the differentiator is how much discretion the executive applies to each.

Washington access did not insulate. A NAIAC seat (2022), a bipartisan advisory council (Aug 2025), a DC office (Mar 2026) and a PAC (Apr 2026) sit on either side of the Feb 27 ban. The thaw ran through Wiles, Bessent, Lutnick and Trump. New government-affairs hires on Aug 4 and Sep 7 add access; the record shows discretion outweighing it.

what.t: Headcount points are few and partly disputed. About 40 staff at the Apr 29, 2022 Series B (T1). Late 2023 reads under 200 or about 500 in two Fortune pieces two days apart, and about 300 per Crunchbase (T3). About 2,300 in Dec 2025 (Fortune, T2), about 2,500 on Jan 30, 2026 (SFist, T3). March 2026 aggregator estimates split at about 3,000 and about 5,000 (T4).

Rahul Patil joined as CTO (Oct 7, 2025, T1; TechCrunch Oct 2) and Sam McCandlish became Chief Architect. On Jan 13, 2026 Mike Krieger moved from CPO to co-lead Labs and Ami Vora took Product (T1). Tino Cuéllar became first Chief Global Affairs Officer on Aug 4 (T1). Reuters' Sep 28 factbox lists eight executives: four founders, four hired since May 2024. The record shows no C-suite exits.

Six directors by appointer: founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, investors' seat Yasmin Razavi, Trust Reed Hastings (May 28, 2025) and Vas Narasimhan (Apr 14, 2026), unstated Chris Liddell (Feb 13, 2026). The board grew from four in May 2024 to seven on Apr 14, 2026, a Trust majority (T1). Trust-appointed Jay Kreps reportedly left May 22 (T5, T4 only). Trustees fell to three when Cuéllar left Aug 4.

Reuters (Sep 28, T2) reviewed a leaked draft prospectus. A Founder LLC of seven co-founders directs one Class F share with 50.1% of votes on key matters. The Trust elects four directors; Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and one other are elected by Class F and Class A holders. The Information, via TechCrunch (Sep 25), adds about 2% each and a three-of-seven minimum-stake test. EDGAR shows no public S-1.

Inbound: Jan Leike (May 2024), John Schulman (Aug 2024), Durk Kingma (Oct 2024), Neil Houlsby from DeepMind (Feb 2025), Andrej Karpathy (May 19, 2026), Dale Finlay from OpenAI (Sep 16, 2026). Schulman left after five months for Mira Murati's startup (T2 relay). Mrinank Sharma (Feb 9, T3) and Jacob Coxon (Sep 8, T2) resigned publicly. Jenny Wen to Cursor rests on a T4 tracker.

Buyback on May 2, 2025: up to 20% of employee shares, $2M per person, two-year tenure, $56.09 a share at $61.5B (T3, single outlet). Tender planned Feb 4, 2026 at $350B pre-money (Bloomberg via aggregator, T3). May 12: Anthropic voided transfers on named secondary platforms (T2). Aug 27: staff may sell inside the IPO and lock-ups may run long (The Information, T4, VERIFY).

means.t: Revenue per head rose because run-rate outran hiring. Run-rate went from about $100M in Sep 2023 (T3, basis unstated) to about $9B at end-2025 (company, gross, T1), roughly 90x, while staff grew 4.6x to at least 11.5x on the disputed base. That is $0.2M-$0.5M per head in late 2023 and $3.9M at end-2025. Recognized FY2025 is $2.0M per head, as recognized revenue trails run-rate in a fast-growing year.

Control sits in two hands. After the IPO the Trust elects 4 of 7 seats. Founders hold 50.1% of votes through Class F, so on this reading they decide the other 3 seats and Class A holders cannot outvote them. Sitting trustees pick new ones with Anthropic, hold no equity, and four of five founding trustees left within 28 months. Post-IPO Class T amendment thresholds are not public.

IPO-readiness hires came in a dated run: CFO Krishna Rao (May 21, 2024), Wilson Sonsini (FT, Dec 2, 2025), ex-Microsoft CFO Chris Liddell to the board (Feb 13, 2026), Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan (Apr 14), confidential S-1 (Jun 1), Cuéllar (Aug 4), legal reshuffle (Aug 26, T4), Matt Clifford (Sep 7, T3). The record ties the policy hires to the Pentagon dispute, so the IPO signal is mixed.

Equity is both the retention lever and the exit risk. Series H ($965B post-money) is 15.7x the May 2025 buyback valuation and 2.6x the tender's pre-money ($900B against $350B). Stock also buys teams: Coefficient Bio, about 10 staff for a reported $400M all-stock, and Runhouse, share-based. The two recorded public resignations cite values, not pay.

implications.t: Hold revenue per head as provisional until the S-1 states headcount. Use $3.9M at end-2025 and $5.6M at Feb 2026, both gross run-rate. The 2,500 versus 5,000 split halves any 2026 figure: annualized Q2 recognized revenue of $46B is $18.4M per head at 2,500 and $9.2M at 5,000. The record has no Q2 headcount.

Treat control as two keys and flag it in both cases. The Trust holds a seat majority by design but has three trustees and, on the best reading, three seated directors today. Founders hold the votes, and the draft warns this could conflict with Class A holders' interests. Price no governance discount until the S-1 shows Class T amendment thresholds, the Class F minimum stake and any sunset.

Rank key-person risk with Daniela Amodei first: Dario Amodei says his only direct report is his chief of staff and all other executives report to her (T3), and she chairs the board. Then Dario Amodei as policy voice, Jared Kaplan (CSO and Responsible Scaling Officer since Oct 2024), Jack Clark (Institute, Mar 11, 2026), Krishna Rao (runs the IPO) and Rahul Patil. Co-founder retention is seven of seven.

Carry employee supply as an unknown, not zero. The record has no lock-up length, no insider-sale size and no stock-compensation figure. Staff may sell inside the offering and lock-ups may exceed the norm (T4, VERIFY). Keep float and overhang as open inputs to the IPO-absorption case until the S-1 states them.

second_order: If the Trust's fourth seat is vacant and Liddell counts as Trust-appointed, the Trust elects three of six today, not a majority. The S-1 board section must show the count. What is easy to miss: the record shows three self-selected trustees, one of whom became an executive, and no Anthropic statement of the split after Apr 14.

Two public resignations on safety grounds (Feb 9, Sep 8), the second 20 days before the leaked prospectus, bracket RSP v3.4 (Jul 8), which cut mandatory sharing of unredacted Risk Reports to at least 200 employees. The record shows no link. S-1 drafters must word key-personnel and dissent risk with care. Liquidity alone will not hold staff whose stated reason is values.

Staff who sold in the tender at $350B pre-money sold at about 39% of the May Series H pre-money, and the IPO is reported at $2T or more. Lock-up expiry, not the IPO, becomes the retention test. Anthropic must carry staff past that date; the record holds no vesting or refresh-grant data and names no outbound move to OpenAI.

Fortune's seven co-founders omit Ben Mann, whom Anthropic's Labs post calls a co-founder, and prospectus coverage does not list the seven. If Mann sits outside the Founder LLC, a Labs co-lead is outside the control bloc. The S-1's named Founder LLC members settle it.

Two UK appointments, Rishi Sunak (Oct 9, 2025) and Matt Clifford (Sep 7, 2026), drew conflict-of-interest questions, and Clifford stays ARIA chair until Nov 6. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion on Sep 25. A policy arm staffed between Aug 4 and Sep 7 may face related-party and adviser disclosure in the S-1.

topics.house_view: (a) Valuation-quality paradox: extends, cannot test; the slice adds a quality datapoint, $3.9M gross run-rate per head at end-2025, but the record has no peer headcount and the comparables table is empty. (b) Equalization ruling: extends; revenue per head inherits Anthropic's gross basis, which OpenAI contests (Apr 13, T2), so any peer comparison needs the same equalization first. (c) IPO absorption: extends; staff selling inside the offering and lock-up length are supply inputs with no figures in the record (T4, VERIFY). (d) Capital efficiency: extends; the record does not say whether tender purchases used company cash or new-round money, so equity raised may partly fund liquidity rather than operations. (e) Sector conventions: extends; founder super-voting precedents (Meta, Snap) do not map one-to-one here, where control is collective, stakes are about 2% each and a purpose Trust elects the seat majority.

topics.title: Ecosystem: investors, partners, customers, acquisitions
topics.one_liner: Reuters' leaked prospectus (T3): Amazon and Google carried 47% of 2025 sales, are owed $221.1B of compute commitments, against equity ceilings near $76B, only Amazon's $18.0B filed.

key_metrics.label: Hyperscaler equity, funded vs announced ceilings
key_metrics.value: $18.0B funded (Amazon 10-Q, T1) inside about $81B of ceilings: Amazon $33.0B, Google $43B, Microsoft $5B. Only Amazon's funding is filed.

key_metrics.label: Public companies tied to Anthropic
key_metrics.value: 118 listed parents by ticker: 29 have an investor role, 16 supply compute, chips or memory, 61 are named customers. Desk flags, not web-verified per row.

key_metrics.label: Compute owed to Amazon, Google and Microsoft
key_metrics.value: $252.5B of $518.2B (48.7%). AMD adds over $20B against up to $5B of equity. About 80% of the total is non-cancelable (Reuters leak: total T2, split T3).

key_metrics.label: Latest enterprise-share datapoint
key_metrics.value: Anthropic 40% vs OpenAI 27% of enterprise LLM API dollars (Menlo, Dec 9 2025, T3, an Anthropic investor). Newer Ramp read: 43.8% vs 39.8% of businesses paying (Sep 9, T4).

key_metrics.label: FY2025 sales routed via Amazon and Google marketplaces
key_metrics.value: 47% ($2.16B), up from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024 (Reuters leak, T3). Two unnamed customers were 12% each (T2).

key_metrics.label: Direct Anthropic equity tickets verified
key_metrics.value: 2 of PitchBook's 35 investments (Goodfire, Sapiom), no check sizes. Largest outbound commitment is $300M to the Ode JV (T2).

what.t: Amazon's 10-Q, Jul 31 (T1): $18.0B funded ($8.0B notes, $5.0B each in Series G and H), $15.0B facility left. Google: over $3B funded by Mar 2025, plus up to $40B, $10B now and $30B on targets (TechCrunch, Apr 24, T2). Microsoft up to $5B, Nvidia up to $10B (Nov 18, T1), AMD up to $5B (Jul 22, T1). Funded amounts for Google's new tranche, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD are absent.

Reuters leak, Sep 29: at least $518B of commitments, about 80% non-cancelable (T2). Split (T3): Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, Microsoft $31.4B, Broadcom-related leases $161.2B, SpaceX up to $84.5B, AMD over $20B. Amazon's $110B is 6.1x its $18.0B funded. Suppliers also pay in equity: Akamai's warrant for up to 5% at $111.33 (T1) and RUM's 50.8M shares at $0.01 (T3).

Reuters leak, Sep 29 (T3): 47% of 2025 sales, $2.16B, ran through Amazon and Google marketplaces, up from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024. They kept about 16 cents a dollar and collected 60% of receivables. Two unnamed customers were 12% each (T2). Snowflake committed $200M (Dec 3, T1). Deloitte's 470,000 seats are 'available to'. Bedrock reports over 100,000 customers (Apr 20, T1).

Closed deals are small. Coefficient Bio ~$400M in stock (Apr 3, T2) and Stainless above $300M (May 18) are single-source; Bun, Vercept, Humanloop and Runhouse are unpriced. Decart (~$6B) and MatX (~$7B) talks lapsed (Sep 8, Aug 27). The $100M Anthology Fund (Jul 17 2024) is Menlo's money. Of PitchBook's 35 investments only Goodfire and Sapiom are direct; Basecamp, Sazabi, Frontier and Theseus are not shown as equity.

Menlo (Dec 9 2025, T3) has Anthropic at 40% of API dollars to OpenAI's 27%. a16z (Jan 30, T3) has OpenAI at 78% in production to Anthropic's 44%. Ramp card data (Aug 20, T3) has 44% to 40% in July, from 41% to 39% in May. Axios (Sep 29, T2, single source) puts OpenAI near $70B run-rate and Anthropic about $65B in July, on different revenue bases.

By ticker. AMZN funder, cloud, channel: $18.0B funded, $110B owed. GOOGL: up to $40B, $111.1B owed. MSFT: up to $5B, $31.4B owed, $3.2B gain (Jul 29, T1). NVDA up to $10B. AMD up to $5B in, over $20B owed. AVGO $10B TPU order. Hosts: WULF $19B, RUM $13.7B, AKAM $11.6B, RIOT $9.1B, HUT $7.0B. Holders: CRM $3.0B (six months), ZM $1.6B (quarter) gains. SPCX $1.25B a month.

means.t: Each hyperscaler is funder, compute seller and channel; Google and Microsoft are also rivals. The equity buys economics without control: Amazon holds non-voting preferred and its notes convert to non-voting common on an IPO, subject to a cap (10-Q, T1). Holders book the mark. Amazon's Q1 gain was $16.8B pre-tax against $30.3B net income, priced by rounds where hyperscalers supplied $15B of Series H's $65B.

Circularity has two legs in the record: equity in from Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD, and compute out to the same names, AMD over $20B against up to $5B. Nvidia sits on both sides at Beacon Point: Lambda installs Nvidia GPUs for Anthropic while Nvidia pays Hut 8 rent (T3). No filing traces cash from an investment to a supplier invoice, so 'circular' is an inference.

Channels run in layers. Cloud marketplaces carried 47% of 2025 sales and kept about 16 cents a dollar, and The Information says Amazon takes roughly half the gross profit on Amazon-routed sales (T3). Anthropic books the sale gross as principal. Snowflake, Databricks and Salesforce bundle Claude. Services firms supply seats 'available to'. Cloud partners collect receivables too, 60% at end-2025 against 42% (Reuters, T3).

The share series measure four different things. Menlo surveyed usage, then estimated dollars. a16z surveyed production breadth. Ramp counts businesses with card spend. OpenRouter counts tokens. Anthropic leads on dollars and card adoption and trails on breadth. Its OpenRouter token share fell to 13.3% from 29.1% (T4). Menlo is an Anthropic investor and Anthropic repeats its 40%, so that figure is not independent.

implications.t: Reprice 'up to' as options. Count only filed dollars as raised: Amazon's $18.0B. Treat Google's $30B as target-gated and Microsoft's $5B, Nvidia's $10B and AMD's $5B as unfunded until a filing says otherwise. Keep four $15B items apart: the Microsoft and Nvidia cap, Series H's hyperscaler share, Amazon's facility and the pre-IPO revolver. Capital efficiency counts equity only, never debt.

Underwrite Amazon and Google as one counterparty on three lines: 47% of 2025 sales as channel, $221.1B as supplier, equity ceilings near $76B as investor. The draft prospectus warns of conflicts of interest with both (T3). Amazon and Google are paid shortfalls, while xAI can exit on 90 days' notice. Ask the S-1 for 2026 channel share and whether $150.0B of named neocloud deals sits above the $518B floor.

Chart shares by basis, never as one line. Tag each point survey, card spend or tokens, and mark Menlo as investor-published. Bulls can cite dollars and card adoption. Bears can cite breadth, 78% vs 44%, and token share. TechCrunch says OpenAI is gaining, but Ramp's May to July figures show Anthropic's lead widening from 2 to 4 points. June is missing.

Rank public exposure by the share of own size the record gives, then by dollars. RUM: contract over 3x market cap (T3). Riot: $9.1B of $9.8B contracted revenue. Amazon: $16.8B Q1 pre-tax gain vs $30.3B net income. Salesforce: 45% of strategic portfolio. Broadcom: $10B order is 13.7% of AI backlog. Then Akamai, TeraWulf, Zoom, Microsoft, Alphabet, AMD, Nvidia. No market caps are computed.

second_order: An IPO near the reported $2T, 2.07x Series H, re-marks every holder again: TheStreet puts Amazon's stake at $300B to $400B against $190.4B carried, and Amazon's notes convert to non-voting common on the IPO, subject to a cap (10-Q, T1). Sell-side must then separate Anthropic marks from AMZN, MSFT, CRM and ZM earnings. The gains recur each priced round, $9.5B in Q3 2025 and $16.8B in Q1 2026.

Nvidia as IPO anchor, up to $10B or about 0.5% at $2T (Reuters, T3), would put a chip supplier in the book while Akamai and RUM already issue Anthropic warrants. Equity then flows both ways between Anthropic and its suppliers. That extends the IPO absorption worry: the price-sensitive float is smaller than the $100B raise, but price discovery is less clean. Underwriters will face related-party questions.

Cursor, Claude's largest coding channel at ARR above $2B, moves under SpaceX in a $60.0B deal. SpaceX rents Anthropic compute on 90-day terms and competes through Grok. Anthropic cut off Windsurf (Jun 2025) and OpenAI (Aug 2025) to avoid supplying rivals. A cut-off would confirm the channel-risk thesis, though Cursor's share of AI-coding spend fell from 41% to about 26% on Ramp data (T3, low confidence).

Each host contract re-rates a small cap in a day: Akamai +17% after hours, Riot +25% after hours, TeraWulf above 10%, RUM +11.6%, while CoreWeave and Nebius fell 5% to 7% on RUM. The missing piece is concentration: Riot's Anthropic lease is 93% of its contracted revenue. If the IPO slips, these names carry the sharpest single-counterparty risk.

Anthropic's six closed deals carry no reported price above about $400M, and two lapsed talks at $6B and $7B sat 50% above Decart's $4B May valuation and 75% above the $4B MatX sought. A $2T stock currency changes the math. A priced deal above $1B would break the pattern and a Decart or MatX revival would reverse the walk-aways. Consensus may be assuming tuck-ins continue.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the market prices unlike quality alike, and Nscale's reported $30B to $35B IPO target rests on $140.6M of H1 revenue and a $1.02B H1 loss, priced off one Anthropic contract whose $44.6B value is press-reported and redacted in its S-1 exhibit. (b) Contradicts in size: marketplace fees were about $351M, 7.6% of FY2025 revenue (Reuters leak, T3), PitchBook sees a 6% to 10% cut from net presentation and The Information forecast 2026 payouts near one-tenth of revenue (both T3), all well below the desk's 39.75% haircut, so unless that haircut nets more than fees this slice does not support it, and Axios's $70B OpenAI against $65B Anthropic still mixes net and gross. (c) Extends: strategic holders are less price-sensitive than the $100B headline raise implies, since Nvidia is reported at up to $10B, Amazon's notes convert to non-voting common on an IPO and its $15.0B facility stays open for 30 months, yet the $2T ask is 2.07x the last mark. (d) Confirms with a wrinkle: $8.0B of Amazon's $18.0B entered as convertible notes, every 'up to' is unfunded, and the $15B revolver and $34.5B TPU SPV notes are debt, so only filed equity counts. (e) Confirms: seats, run-rate and contract value mean different things across software, cloud and hosting, since Deloitte's 470,000 is 'available to' and RUM's $13.7B is six-year contract value.

uncertainties.note: Funded versus up-to. Only Amazon's $18.0B is filed. Google's $10B first tranche is reported as made but unconfirmed, and Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD funded amounts are absent. Amazon's ownership is 15% to 20% (TheStreet, T3), about 21% (Forkast, T4) or 19.7% by desk arithmetic; no filing states it.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Alphabet, Microsoft and Nvidia filings, or the capitalization table in the public S-1.

uncertainties.note: The $518.2B total is T2, but the six-partner split and the channel figures rest on one Reuters chain, T3 in the prospectus facts table. None of the $150.0B of named neocloud contracts (Nscale, Lambda, TeraWulf, RUM, Akamai, Volta, Riot, Hut 8) is among the six, so $518B is probably a floor, though the draft may predate or fold them in. SpaceX is $40B, $45B or up to $84.5B by source. Nscale's S-1 exhibit redacts value, and TeraWulf and Riot do not name Anthropic.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The commitments table and related-party note in the public S-1.

uncertainties.note: Circularity is an inference. The record shows equity in and compute out for the same names, and warrants flowing back from Akamai and RUM, but no filing traces cash from an investment to an invoice. Amazon's 10-Q says its AWS commercial arrangement was amended, terms not given. The leaked FY2025 net loss of $42B includes a ~$34B non-cash remeasurement of convertible financing (T2); holders book gains on similar instruments, and the record does not link the two.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: S-1 use-of-proceeds, related-party and financial-instrument notes.

uncertainties.note: Share series are not like-for-like. Menlo is an Anthropic investor, and 40% of its $12.5B API pool is about $5.0B for 2025 against $3.8B of usage-based revenue in the leaked prospectus (T3), on different bases. Ramp restated May from 34.4% to 41%, and the Sep read is T4. The 2026 channel share and the names of the two 12% customers are not in the record.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Ramp's primary tables, an independent spend survey, or the S-1 revenue split by product and channel.

uncertainties.note: IPO re-mark. Reference class: the three priced rounds since Sep 2025 each lifted holders' marks, Amazon's preferred from $14.8B at Dec 2025 to $92.5B at Jun 2026. A base rate for mega-IPO pricing against the last private mark is not in the record. What differs: $2T is 2.07x Series H and timing is October in some reports and November in WSJ (T3).
